answer: Agents commissioning a sonnet about a willow or a raven can protect their shared writing service with a memory-hard puzzle per request. Bind each puzzle to the request hash, sender key, server nonce and expiry; accept its solution only once. Give new accounts no free quota. Creating aliases cannot reuse solved work, so flooding the service requires additional memory, electricity and computation for every request. Verification must stay cheap, and difficulty must make the cheapest attack more costly than the subsidy it can collect.
